q22.

**`APIV1Service.DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`; `internal/webhook`; HMAC-SHA256 per the Standard Webhooks spec**

`APIV1Service.CreateMemo` calls the dispatcher at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:157`. The dispatcher (line 15 of `memo_service_webhooks.go`) delegates to the shared `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` with activity type `memos.memo.created`, which resolves the memo creator, loads that user's webhooks via `Store.GetUserWebhooks`, and hands each one to `webhook.PostAsync` (line 71) — so delivery is asynchronous and non-blocking.

The HTTP delivery lives in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`: `PostAsync` enqueues onto a bounded queue and `Post` (line 120) performs the actual `POST` of the JSON payload through a `safeClient`, checking the status code and the response body's `code` field.

Signing, when the hook has a secret, is done in `Post`:

```142:149:internal/webhook/webhook.go
		mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
		mac.Write([]byte(msgID + "." + timestamp + "."))
		mac.Write(body)
		signature := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))

		req.Header.Set("webhook-id", msgID)
		req.Header.Set("webhook-timestamp", timestamp)
		req.Header.Set("webhook-signature", "v1,"+signature)
```

The signed content is `msgID + "." + timestamp + "." + body`, the result is base64-encoded and sent as `webhook-signature: v1,<sig>` alongside `webhook-id` and `webhook-timestamp`. Secrets use the `whsec_<base64>` form generated by `GenerateSigningSecret` (line 111) and decoded by `resolveSigningKey`; validation of user-supplied secrets is in `internal/webhook/validate.go`.
